newsitem.title: UK: British retail prices rise 2.9 percent in June.
newsitem.headline: British retail prices rise 2.9 percent in June.

text.p: Britain's retail prices rose 2.9 percent in the year to June from 2.6 percent in May, official figures showed on Tuesday.
Inflation, minus the effect of mortgage interest repayments, was 2.7 percent in June after 2.5 percent in May. The figures were above analysts' expectations.
Government bond prices dropped after the data. Analysts said they underlined the market's belief that interest rates would be raised by the Bank of England at a regular meeting later this week.
Shares remained under pressure but sterling set a 73-month high, rising a pfennig to 2.97 marks, supported by the interest rate outlook.

"A disappointing set of figures.. Petrol prices and motoring costs in general might have been pushing the figure up," said Nigel Richardson, head of bond research at Yamaichi International Europe. Official interest rates are currently at 6.50 percent.
